# Kayak Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/kayak-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/kayak-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects flight data from kayak.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Kayak Flight Prices in 2026](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-kayak)
- **Code:** [`kayak.py`](kayak.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Oneway](results/oneway.json) · [Roundtrip](results/roundtrip.json)

## What it scrapes

- Kayak flight search results (round-trip and one-way)
- Flight price, airline code, departure/arrival times, and booking options
- Search metadata (search ID, filtered/total counts, pages scraped)

## Functions

- `scrape_flights(origin, destination, departure_date, return_date=None, sort='bestflight_a', max_pages=10)` → `List[Dict[str, Any]]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/oneway.json`](results/oneway.json): `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `trip_type`, `currency`, `carrier`, `departure_time`, `arrival_time`, `duration`, `stops`, `price`, `provider_deal_count`, `captured_at`
- [`results/roundtrip.json`](results/roundtrip.json): `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `trip_type`, `currency`, `carrier`, `departure_time`, `arrival_time`, `duration`, `stops`, `price`, `provider_deal_count`, `captured_at`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`kayak.py`](kayak.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Notes

Kayak.com can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking, so this scraper uses Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature, browser rendering, and session-based requests to capture and paginate Kayak's internal flights poll API.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/kayak-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_scrape_roundtrip`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
